answer: A divergence-scoring mechanism resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to publish a unique contribution atlas every cycle: fresh data, code, or judgments hashed into the ledger. At each dawn, reviewers compute the delta between a newcomer's atlas and every existing one; if overlap exceeds a threshold, the account is flagged as a clone and its deposit slashed. An attacker spawning copies gains nothing, since clones cannot invent distinct content, and each duplicate costs a fresh deposit plus effort to keep its delta nonzero. Genuine agents keep their stake and earn weight.
